candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record points specifically to syphilitic aortitis: ascending aortic involvement with echogenic shadows (calcification/gumma), aortic insufficiency, slit-like left main ostial stenosis, and absence of atherosclerosis are classic features of tertiary syphilis. Treponema pallidum is listed first among the causative organisms under investigation. C001 correctly identifies infectious aortitis of the ascending aorta but omits the syphilitic (treponemal) etiology required by the benchmark reference, making it a parent category rather than a complete equivalent.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Infectious aortitis of the ascending aorta is the parent category; syphilitic aortitis (Treponema pallidum etiology) is the required specific subtype

case_quality_flags: Classic triad of syphilitic aortitis present: aortic regurgitation, coronary ostial stenosis, and ascending aortic involvement with calcification
